01-cube.caption: The complete construction on the cube. (a) The square-in-square cube has a degree-two subgraph with two cycles. (b) Its dual is the octahedron, in the disk embedding used below; shaded faces are black and hollow vertices are roots. (c) Outlined choices $r$ and solid choices $s$ are disjoint states; the arrows $r(t)\to s(t)$ form $D$. (d) The sides opposite $s$ form the forest $Q_s$. (e) Delete the dotted chosen spokes. The remaining spokes form a tree; the dual edges across deleted spokes form the white-face tree, rooted at the ring. (f) That tree selects one bold side per face. The selected edges $P$ induce two trees, and their complementary dual is one Hamiltonian cycle.
01-cube.drawn_from: cube and octahedron; all objects from check.octahedron()

02-two-factors.caption: Degree two does not ensure one cycle. The running graph $G$ has $22$ vertices; filled and hollow dots are its bipartition. Both bold subgraphs have degree two everywhere, but only the connected one in (b) is Hamiltonian. The same embedding is used for the final cycle in Figure~13.
02-two-factors.drawn_from: G = dual of running.json; (a) a 2-factor with two components, (b) the cycle recovered in Figure 13

03-dual.caption: Pass from $G$ to $T=G^*$. Grey edges join face centres across their corresponding edges of $T$. Shaded faces are black, including the outer face $t_0$ shown by the collar. The hollow roots are $0,4,5$; the $10$ bounded black faces match the $10$ nonroot vertices.
03-dual.drawn_from: running.json with the disk layout; vertex numbers are those of running.json

04-local.caption: Read the two choices inside one black triangle $t$. The outlined corner is $r(t)$, the solid corner is $s(t)$, and the third is $u(t)$. The solid arrow is $D$, while the dashed opposite side is $Q_s$. In (b), replacing the edge by two spokes gives weight $a(t,s(t))-a(t,r(t))$ and excludes $u(t)$ from the tinted subdisk.
04-local.drawn_from: schematic of one triangle, no computed object

05-state.caption: A state is a perfect matching between the bounded black triangles $A$ and the nonroot vertices $X$. In (a), each solid choice belongs to its shaded triangle. In (b), the same choices are solid incidence edges; the double edges give the disjoint state $r$. Together $r+s$ has degree two at every square and dot.
05-state.drawn_from: s and r = the displayed pair (check.running)

06-flow.caption: The incidence flow supplies a pair. Source and sink edges have capacity $2$; incidence edges have capacity $1$. The displayed integral flow has value $2|X|=20$. Its used incidences have degree two at every vertex and triangle, so alternating along cycles splits them into states $r,s$. The cut inequality is tight at $S=\{2\}$.
06-flow.drawn_from: incidence graph of running.json; cut inequality (3.1) checked for all 1024 subsets S

07-pair-D.caption: (a) Two states that choose different corners in every bounded black triangle. (b) Join the outlined corner to the solid corner in each triangle. Every vertex other than a root has one arrow in and one arrow out, so the arrows form disjoint directed cycles. Here $D$ is a counterclockwise cycle of length $7$ and a clockwise triangle.
07-pair-D.drawn_from: the displayed pair; D-cycles from check.running

08-disk.caption: Count the tinted disk of the long $D$-cycle. It contains $B=5$ black faces, $W=6$ white faces and $I=3$ ringed vertices. Each outlined choice lies at an interior vertex or at the tail of a marked boundary arrow, giving $B=I+\ell$. Combine this with the two face counts to get $2\ell-h=-3$.
08-disk.drawn_from: disk of the 7-cycle of D(r,s); counts and the face-by-face matching from check.running

09-Q.caption: The opposite sides distinguish failure from success. (a) The second state $s$ of Figure~7 gives a cycle of $Q_s$ around the central white triangle. (b) The first state $r$, now drawn solid, gives a forest with one root per component. Recovery uses the pair $(s,r)$.
09-Q.drawn_from: Q_s and Q_r for the displayed pair; one root per component asserted

10-cancellation.caption: Keep $s$ fixed and reverse the heavy dashed cycle of $Q_s$. Only the outlined choices move, from $r$ to $\tilde r$; the solid choices and $\omega(s)$ stay fixed. The disk identity changes $J$ by $2$, so the phases are opposite and the two terms $i^J e^{x\omega(s)}$ cancel.
10-cancellation.drawn_from: reversal of the Q_s cycle (Lemma 5.2); J values and involution asserted

11-spokes.caption: Slide each dashed cycle of $D$ onto its solid spoke route. Unit circulation around each bounded spoke face makes the counterclockwise weight difference $L^+-L^-$ equal to the white-face count inside the original cycle, labelled $W$. Both counts are positive. Each cycle gives a simple zero, so this group has a nonzero leading term of phase $(-i)^2$.
11-spokes.drawn_from: unit spoke circulations solved in check.spoke_weights; L+ - L- = W asserted for both cycles

12-tree-cotree.caption: Recover from the forest state $r$ of Figure~9(b), drawn solid. (a) Delete the dotted chosen spokes; the remaining spokes, joined through $c_0$, form a spanning tree. (b) Each deleted spoke is crossed at its midpoint by one edge of the white-face tree. Its root $y_0$ is the ringed face across $e_0=\{0,4\}$.
12-tree-cotree.drawn_from: H - r is a tree, white-face tree is a tree (check.recover)

13-selected.caption: The white-face tree selects the bold sides. Its root selects $e_0$; each other white face selects the side towards its parent. Every black and white face has one selected side. The resulting $P$ is a forest with two components. Its complementary dual in (b) is one cycle through all $22$ faces, separating the disk and square classes into two induced trees.
13-selected.drawn_from: P, the two induced trees and the Hamiltonian cycle (check.recover asserts each property)

14-gluing.caption: Glue across the separating triangle $\{3,4,5\}$. Solve the outer piece first, then prescribe its same-class edge $\{3,5\}$ on the inner piece. The classes agree on the cap. For each class the two trees meet in that edge or in vertex $4$, so their union is again an induced tree.
14-gluing.drawn_from: two octahedra glued along a face (check.gluing asserts both glued classes induce trees)

15-overview.caption: The order of the argument and where each figure belongs. Solid boxes are the main line for a triangulation without separating triangles. The disk identity is used twice, for the cancellation and for the forest of selected edges. Separating triangles are handled last, by induction.
15-overview.drawn_from: logical dependence of Sections 2 to 7 of the OpenAI paper (LIT), no computed object

16-at-a-glance.caption: The proof at a glance on the running example. Read the strip from left to right. Cancellation removes cyclic second states; nonvanishing supplies a forest state. The white-face tree then selects the forest whose complementary dual is the Hamiltonian cycle.
16-at-a-glance.drawn_from: running example; all states, cycles, white-tree and P from check.running; general implications LIT OpenAI Sections 2--7
